evidence: git log shows no commit touching either package directory since 4ea389a; worktree clean; zero tracked-file change.

The walker delta between old and new rules is exclusively *.pyc bytecode: 12 files (harmonic-invariants) and 11 files (court-filter-algebra), including coexisting pytest-8.4.2 and pytest-9.1.1 artifacts regenerated across runs; .pyc embeds source mtimes, so the old expectation was inherently unreproducible.

Recomputation under the new rule (module scripts/manifest-utils.mjs frozenPayloadExcluded, graph/runtime/canonical.mjs canonicalJsonBytes) reproduces the repository-stable values above; walker-verified tracked-only inputs (untracked non-cache files: none).
The new rule matches the landed manifest convention (scripts/build-manifest.mjs:13-34 excludes the same caches; validate:manifest PASS).

q1.resolution: Re-canonicalization as housekeeping under OD-083-3; expectations updated at commit 1b19d2f with the root-cause message; frozen payload checks restored to 7/7.

The failure is entirely the deployment-roundtrip leg: the committed qa/neo4j-deployment-roundtrip-validation.json is a live FAIL 1/2 receipt stamped seven-governors-integrated-1.9.0-dev (configured-roundtrip FAIL, normalizedSnapshot null), so releaseId === 1.8.1, verdict PASS, 3/0 and both snapshot-equality conjuncts fail.

q2.mechanism: The retained baseline is release-stamped by design: the deployment/full verify compares the live snapshot against provenance/neo4j-full-database-baseline.json (namespace fingerprints and provenance/release.json source binding), so a development cycle cannot pass the retained-baseline check; the 67dcd14 failure was deterministic, not incidental.
q2.classification: release-scope policy with technical execution: the baseline lifecycle question (retain 1.8.1 vs re-baseline at close) required a maintainer ruling; the receipt overwrite is fixable tooling behavior.
q2.resolution: OD-083-1: re-baseline to 1.9.0 at close (Path B), following the GOV-501 precedent; release-state update, not a data change (six projected payload namespaces byte-identical; counts 3061/10506).
